solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unconnected notes placed on record

indicators.note: the notes are set down after the record, joined on to it

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
re and te are two notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone jots down separate musical notes onto a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means separate and distinct, so things that are not joined to one another.

clue.text: One surprisingly successful alternative clue to 15?

definitions.meaning: an unexpected winner, little known beforehand
15 down is a bad dream; dark can stand for night and horse for mare, so the words clue it another way

explanation.surface: A setter proposes a different way of cluing another entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider who wins unexpectedly is a long-standing racing idiom; the second sense is wordplay for night plus mare.

clue.text: French writer not one to put up with computer game

parts.note: a sim is a simulation computer game

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: not one means none

explanation.surface: A French author who won't tolerate video games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put up' reverses NONE to ENON.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Simenon was the Belgian-born, French-language creator of Maigret.

clue.text: Rib available for stew

parts.note: to rib is to tease, to rag
out as in on sale or released, as a newly published book is

explanation.surface: A rib of meat on offer for a casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a highly seasoned French meat and vegetable stew.

clue.text: Bluish article goes out in Brewers

parts.note: teal is a greenish-blue colour
a is the indefinite article
a fire or light dies when it goes out

explanation.surface: A blue-tinted item is dropped among beer makers.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea ladies were women who made and served tea in British offices.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who make the office tea are people who brew, hence a witty sense of brewers.

clue.text: Grant for recruit

definitions.note: to grant is to transfer or allot something formally to someone

parts.note: as can mean for, in the role of, as in 'take this as payment'
to sign a player is to recruit them

explanation.surface: Money given for taking on new staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign property or rights is to transfer them formally, a synonym of allot or award.

clue.text: State capital — something valuable to blow on centre for trade

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold, a valuable thing
a gust is a blow of wind

indicators.note: only the central letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Financial jargon about blowing a valuable asset on a trading hub.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is the capital city of the US state of Maine.

clue.text: Rock covers are irritating, then diverting

indicators.note: the word for rock goes round the irritation

parts.note: to rock is to sway or swing
itch as a plural verb means are irritating, tickle

explanation.surface: Rock music cover versions that grate but still entertain.
explanation.definitionFit: Switching a train or a stream sends it on another course, which is diverting it.

clue.text: One memorably sent up doting father, finally, at home

parts.note: gaga means senile, doting

indicators.note: the end letter of the word for father is used

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A fond old dad remembered for being mocked in his own house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' looks like mocked, but means launched into space.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuri Gagarin, the Soviet cosmonaut, was the first person launched into space, in 1961.

clue.text: Not all returned from Irish border

indicators.note: the run of letters is read backwards
only some of the letters of these two words are used, a run straddling them

explanation.surface: Something brought back from the Irish frontier, but not the whole of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not all' takes MIR from the end of 'from' and start of 'Irish'; 'returned' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rim is the edge or border of something round, such as a cup or wheel.

clue.text: Fool endlessly pleading not to be taken

indicators.note: the word for fool loses its final letter

parts.note: a goat is a fool, as in 'play the goat'
begging means pleading

explanation.surface: A clown who keeps on begging but refuses to be captured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the T from GOAT, leaving GOA.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something available that nobody wants, left unclaimed.

clue.text: Hospital's nurses moving around country

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so H and S hold the other letters between them

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, and the 's gives S

indicators.note: the letters of 'around' are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Hospital staff bustling about the ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' looks like hospital staff, but it is the signal that H and S cradle the jumbled word.
explanation.definitionFit: Honduras is a republic in Central America.

clue.text: Hands get better fast

parts.note: S and E, South and East, are two hands (players) at bridge
to cure is to make better, restoring health

explanation.surface: Workers recover quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players, or hands, are North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast in the sense of firmly fixed, as in 'hold fast', is a synonym for firmly attached.

clue.text: Seeing red, not silver, item of jewellery

indicators.note: the silver is to be left out of the word for furious

parts.note: seeing red means furious, raging
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A furious person who rejects a silver piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring is a band worn on the finger as an ornament.

clue.text: What's given pear, extraordinarily?

indicators.note: something done out of the ordinary way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about who was handed a pear.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a grape plant would only produce a pear by extraordinary means, and it bears unexpected fruit as the rumour mill.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant bears grapes, and the word also means the informal network that passes on rumours.

clue.text: Falsification of tax is no sin for US confederacy

indicators.note: falsifying something distorts it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheat insisting that fiddling one's taxes is no wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iroquois league of Native American peoples in New York State is known by this name; it is also rugby's tournament.

clue.text: A thing to disturb, with REM?

definitions.text: A thing to disturb, with REM?

indicators.note: disturbing these letters puts them in a different order

explanation.surface: Something that troubles one during the dreaming phase of sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: REM is rapid eye movement, the sleep phase in which dreams occur; the whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A frightening dream disturbs sleep and typically comes in the dreaming phase.

clue.text: Show offender using smack consuming wine with judge

indicators.note: the blow swallows the wine and the judge

parts.note: to sock is to hit, smack
hock is German white wine

explanation.surface: A criminal who hits someone after downing wine with a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio host who sets out to offend listeners for attention is a broadcaster of this sort.

clue.text: Son's squealing after jumping across parallel bars

indicators.note: the jumbled letters stretch across, enclosing the abbreviation for son
the letters of 'squealing' are jumbled once they have jumped about

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A boy shrieks after leaping over gymnastic apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parallel bars' looks gymnastic, but means the two short lines of the mathematical symbol; 'across' has the jumbled letters span S.
explanation.definitionFit: The mathematical symbol for equality is drawn as two short horizontal parallel lines.

clue.text: Mention about academy being not short of members

indicators.note: the word for mention goes about, around, the academy

parts.note: to quote is to cite or mention
RA is the Royal Academy

explanation.surface: A citation about an academy that has its full complement.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting is quorate when enough members are present for business to proceed.

clue.text: Cap is right on old man, filling figure out

indicators.note: the pair goes inside, filling the word for figure out

parts.note: to suss is slang for to work out

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: pa is father, one's old man

explanation.surface: Someone is right about their father and fills in a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To cap a story is to outdo or beat it, to go one better.

clue.text: Benefit payment an attempt to take in the taxman, once

indicators.note: the attempt surrounds the old tax office

parts.note: to have a go is to make an attempt
IR is the Inland Revenue, the former UK tax authority

explanation.surface: A claimant tries to sneak a welfare cheque past the tax inspector.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a giro was a cheque by which state benefits were paid.
explanation.definitionFit: British welfare money was formerly paid by a cheque of this kind, so the word came to mean the payment itself.

clue.text: Island one female short for holding dance: not good!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the shortened woman holds the shortened dance
the word for female is short of its last letter

parts.note: a woman is a female

indicators.note: the abbreviation for good is to be left out of the dance

parts.note: a jig is a lively dance

explanation.surface: An islander, one woman short of a dance partner, laments that it's no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts N from WOMAN to WOMA; 'not good' takes G from JIG, leaving JI, which WOMA holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Iwo Jima is the Japanese Pacific island famous for its Second World War battle.

clue.text: Rising pop celebrity upset old primate

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for father reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: pop is father, pa

indicators.note: the word for celebrity is turned upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: a name is a famous person, as in 'a big name'

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming pop star upset an elderly ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns PA to AP; 'upset' turns NAME to EMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A hominid intermediate between apes and humans was a supposed early ancestor of humankind.

clue.text: Regret bribe taken the wrong way affected one

indicators.note: the pair of words is read backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret
a sop is something given to pacify, a bribe

explanation.surface: Someone who regrets a bribe that was misunderstood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken the wrong way' turns RUESOP into POSEUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who puts on airs and behaves affectedly to impress others is a show-off of this sort.

clue.text: Busy with oxygen in supply tap

indicators.note: the policeman and the oxygen go inside the word for supply

parts.note: a stock is a supply of goods
a busy is British slang for a police officer, a PC (police constable)
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A policeman with an oxygen cylinder fits into a supply line.
explanation.definitionFit: A valve on a water pipe that can be turned off is a kind of tap.

clue.text: Story of Napoleon's rise, using brute force and power

parts.note: a brute is a beast, an animal
F is the abbreviation for force in physics
arm in the sense of power or might, as in the arm of the law

explanation.surface: A history of the emperor's ascent by sheer brutality and might.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon is the pig who seizes control in Orwell's novel, not the French emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's allegory tells how the pig named Napoleon rises to rule the farm.

clue.text: Tongue is bright orange, first of all

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the three words is taken

explanation.surface: A tongue that is a vivid orange colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibo, or Igbo, is a language spoken in Nigeria.

clue.text: Headgear concerned with stopping hazards

indicators.note: the short word plugs a gap, sitting inside the gambles

parts.note: a hazard is a gamble or bet
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Hats worried about blocking dangers.
explanation.definitionFit: Berets are soft round flat caps, a kind of hat.

clue.text: Check report of end of dry spell on radio?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so these words are a sound
radio is heard rather than seen, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: a dry spell ends when the rain comes back

explanation.surface: A weather broadcaster confirms the drought is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull on the reins slows a horse, hence to restrain or hold in check.
